sections.text: An enum is a type that can be one of a fixed set of variants. Use it when a value can only be one of a few things.
Variants can carry data, and each variant can carry different data:
Enums can have methods too. To do something different for each variant, use match, which you'll learn properly in the last lesson of this unit:
An enum is like a multiple-choice answer: the value is exactly one of the listed options, never something else.
Rust enums are tagged unions (sum types), much richer than C or Java enums. Together with structs they let you make invalid states unrepresentable.

exercise.prompt: Add a fourth variant, Mythic, to Rarity and make the program print it. It should print: Mythic

quiz.question: How many variants can an enum value be at one time?
How do you write the East variant of Direction?
Can different variants of the same enum carry different data?
